title: Croatia's Inflation Falls but Households Remain Under Pressure · 20 Aug
keywords: Croatia, inflation, cost of living, fuel prices, eurozone, ECB, price caps, energy intervention, European Union, household finances, monetary policy, Zagreb
notes: Croatia's annual inflation slowed to 3.9% in July, offering tentative relief after months of sharp price rises, but the figure still sits well above the European Central Bank's 2% target. The government points to falling headline numbers as proof that its policies are working, while critics argue that everyday costs remain painfully high. A parallel debate over state-mandated fuel price caps is sharpening questions about whether Zagreb is delivering lasting economic stability or merely managing the appearance of one.
